results.title: Obuasi East ambulance returns to service after five years off the road
results.content: Residents of the Obuasi East Municipality are set to benefit from improved emergency medical transportation after the municipal ambulance was restored to service following a GH¢50,000 donation by the Chief Executive Officer of Obuasi Beverages, Dr Collins Amo. The contribution went towards replacing the vehicle’s faulty engine and repairing it after it had remained off the road for nearly five years. The repaired ambulance was formally presented to Dr Amo by the Obuasi East Municipal Ambulance Director, SAEMT Irene Cynthia Akornor, who thanked him for supporting the restoration. Dr Amo expressed satisfaction with the vehicle’s return to service and called for greater private-sector participation in addressing critical community needs.

results.title: Kumasi Central Prison holds 1,600 inmates against 500 capacity as authorities intensify decongestion
results.content: The Kumasi Central Prison is holding an average of 1,600 inmates, more than three times its authorised capacity of 500, as the Ashanti Regional Prisons Command steps up efforts to ease overcrowding. The facility, built in 1901, is among the prisons facing pressure from rising inmate numbers, with remand prisoners identified as a major contributor to the congestion. The regional command is pursuing a multi-pronged decongestion strategy involving inmate transfers, closer coordination with the police and judiciary, and interventions under the Justice for All Programme. Chief Superintendent Richard Bukari, the Ashanti Regional Prisons Service Public Relations Officer, said the command regularly transfers eligible inmates to camp prisons to reduce pressure on congested facilities. results.title: ADB Ghana installs advanced DNA equipment at Noguchi Institute
results.content: ADB Ghana Medical Systems Group, through Thermo Fisher Scientific UK, has installed advanced DNA equipment at the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research to strengthen Ghana’s capacity for human identification and forensic investigations. The equipment forms part of the newly commissioned National Human Identification Laboratory, which is expected to improve the institute’s capacity to analyse DNA, identify human remains and support investigations requiring scientific confirmation of identity. President John Dramani Mahama commissioned the facility on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as part of efforts to expand Ghana’s local capacity for forensic analysis and human identification.
